test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 03 Oct, 2023 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: According to the Census of India 2011, what was the percentage of Sikh communities in the total population in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1.7%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Census of India 2011,** the percentage of Sikh communities in the total population in India was **1.7%**.
 
• The Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, has unveiled the data concerning the Population by Religious Communities as per the Census of 2011.
 
• The distribution encompasses the total population categorized across six major religious communities: Hindu, Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, and Jain, along with classifications for "Other Religions and Persuasions" and "Religion not stated."
 
• The data delineates the population figures by sex and residence, extending to sub-districts and towns.
 
• As per the findings, the total population in 2011 stood at 121.09 crores. Among the major religious communities, Hindus accounted for 96.63 crores (79.8%), followed by Muslims with 17.22 crores (14.2%), Christians with 2.78 crores (2.3%), Sikhs with 2.08 crores (1.7%), Buddhists with 0.84 crores (0.7%), and Jains with 0.45 crores (0.4%).
 
• Additionally, "Other Religions & Persuasions" comprised 0.79 crores (0.7%) of the population, while 0.29 crores (0.2%) fell under the category of Religion Not Stated.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In the decade spanning from 2001 to 2011, several noteworthy changes have occurred in the proportions of various religious communities within the total population of India.
 
• The proportion of the Hindu population to the total population experienced a decline of 0.7 percentage points (PP) during this period.
 
• Similarly, the Sikh population witnessed a decrease of 0.2 PP, while the Buddhist population declined by 0.1 PP.
 
• Conversely, the proportion of the Muslim population to the total population observed an increase of 0.8 PP, indicating a notable demographic shift.
